title: Smørrebrød with Pickled Herring, Onion and Dill
summary: Thin slices of dark rye bread buttered to the edges and covered with pickled herring, red onion rings, optional egg and dill. Ready in 10 minutes and eaten with a knife and fork.

ingredients.item: thin slices dense dark rye bread (rugbrød), about 1 cm thick
pickled herring fillets in a plain vinegar marinade, drained
small red onion, sliced into thin rings

ingredients.note: boiled 10 min to a firm yolk

steps.title: Trim the bread
steps.text: Cut the rye into neat rectangles about 8 x 12 cm.

steps.title: Butter
steps.text: Spread the butter thinly right to the edges. It adds richness and stops the topping soaking into the bread.

steps.title: Add the herring
steps.text: Pat the herring dry, cut it into bite-size pieces and lay them close together so they cover the bread completely. Tuck the onion rings and egg slices in between.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Scatter with dill and a little pepper and serve straight away, with a knife and fork.

tips: Danes eat herring first, then other fish, then meat and cheese.
Curried herring or herring in a creamy dill sauce are tasty alternatives.
Choose herring in a plain vinegar and sugar marinade.
storage: Assemble just before serving. Opened herring keeps in its marinade in the fridge for up to 1 week. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
